figures.title: The final method
figures.caption: The selected CN-only tool: covariate-adjusted trans association with leave-own-chromosome-out arm adjustment, a cis-instrument gate and co-segment attribution, with an optional context layer; both outputs are evaluated against held-out CRISPRi Perturb-seq.

figures.title: Why the benchmark is hard
figures.caption: Perturb-seq trans hits are concentrated in a few perturbations (top 10% carry 96% of HCT116 and 97% of HEK293T TRAIN hits), and in HEK293T most hits come from perturbations whose gene is not even expressed, so HCT116 is the primary line.

figures.title: Held-out design
figures.caption: Regulators were split by whole chromosome arm: 28 TRAIN arms (3,806 HCT116 regulators) for all tuning and 14 TEST arms (1,817 regulators) whose Perturb-seq labels were sealed until the single final run.

figures.title: How the method was chosen
figures.caption: On HCT116 TRAIN, the cis-instrument gate (G1) and co-segment attribution (A3) raised the top-0.1% odds ratio from 1.59 to 5.00; every other candidate was rejected, and the context layer (24.1) was reported but not selected because a within-regulator pair shuffle kept its gain.

figures.title: Held-out TEST results
figures.caption: On HCT116 TEST the selected CN-only tool reaches OR 3.85 (jackknife CI 1.33–11.2; pre-registered permutation p = 0.068), numerically below the target-detectability, co-expression and hub baselines (no paired difference significant), and it does not replicate in HEK293T.

figures.title: Direction of predicted effects: not established
figures.caption: The selected tool's sign concordance (71.8% vs a within-regulator null of 64.7%, p = 0.012, n = 131) looks better than chance, but the permuted-CN control C2 passes the same test (58.5% vs 53.2%, p = 0.001, n = 354), so the test is miscalibrated and the direction result is not established; it is also not significant in S1 or no-split-sibling regulators.

figures.title: What signal there is concerns which regulators, not which targets
figures.caption: Shuffling scores among each regulator's targets leaves the TEST odds ratio almost unchanged (3.85 → 3.76; context layer 18.4 → 17.3) and per-regulator AUROC at 0.50, whereas permuting copy number, which changes which regulators score high, lowers it (1.28; context fusion 10.6). For the CN-only tool that drop is not significant (paired Δlog-OR +1.10, CI −0.66 to 2.85); for the context layer it is (+0.55, CI 0.07–1.03).

figures.title: Project journey
figures.caption: The whole project ran in about 5.4 hours of commits on 27 Oct 2026: design frozen after three review rounds, TEST labels sealed before any evaluation, two tuning steps adopted on TRAIN, a context layer rejected by its control, then one locked TEST run and an independent report check.
